newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA RUPIAH DRIVEN LOWER BY STOCK MARKET FALL.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA RUPIAH DRIVEN LOWER BY STOCK MARKET FALL.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was driven lower against the dollar in midday trading on Thursday after the stock market plunged almost three percent, dealers said.
They said the composite index tumbled 2.9 percent to 679.54 points in the morning session, spilling over to the foreign exchange market and knocking the rupiah down.
Spot rupiah fell to 2,595/2,602 at 0615 GMT from an opening of 2,586.0/91.0.
"The rupiah was well bid at 2,585 in the morning and suddenly during Jakarta lunch break the rupiah falls to 2,595 level," one European bank dealer said.
One U.S. bank dealer said it was mainly due to spillover from the stock market which caused some profit-taking in the dollar-rupiah market and probably some stop-loss covering.
"But volume is pretty thin," the dealer said.
Stock brokers said the plunge was due to new margin rules from the Capital Markets Supervisory Agency (Bapepam) which forced investors to cut their holdings.
"This seems to have caused heavy unloading and triggered further liquidation as many of them could not meet margin calls," one major local broker said.
Among the new rules, Bapepam required margin investors to provide a deposit of at least 50 percent of the value of share purchases. Previously margins could be as high as one-for-five.
Brokers said they were also forcing investors to cut their holdings to meet Bapepam's requirements in order to obtain a margin license from the authority.

Currency dealers said the rupiah was on the road to recovery in the morning, attempting to break the 2,580 resistance level, before the impact of the stock market plunge spilled over into the currency markets.
